newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian airport workers begin one-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Italian airport workers begin one-day strike.

text.p: Airport workers in Italy began a one-day strike on Tuesday over demands for more pay, forcing state carrier Alitalia to cancel 143 flights.
The strike by 15,000 workers forced Alitalia to cancel the national and international flights scheduled for Tuesday. Airport officials said foreign airlines will also be hit.
Unions called the strike to try to force the government to replace old pay contracts, which expired in June 1995.
In a full-page advertisement in Italian newspapers on Tuesday, Alitalia promised to do everything possible to minimise the impact on passengers.

"With an exceptional mobilisation of its ground and air personnel, Alitalia will try to reduce to the minimum the disruptions to its clientele caused by an airport workers' strike planned for today," the carrier said.
